claims.assertion: The $6.61 arose as a driver-cancelled no-show, so it can only stand if NS-1 (i)-(iii) are all satisfied; NS-0/NS-2 govern this branch.

NS-1 (ii) fails on the system records: the closest the driver ever came to the pickup point was 319 m at 08:46:50 and he was never within 200 m (F1), and the timeline never records driver_arrived_at the pickup (F4).

NS-1 (iii) also fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while 351 m from the pickup and then spent 0 s within 200 m, and his 4-minute stationary period (08:47:00-08:51:00) was at a point 350 m from the pickup, not at the pickup point.

The free-waiting period cannot rescue the fee either: the driver's patience ran only 7 minutes from acceptance (08:44:00) to cancellation (08:51:00) and the stationary wait was 4 min 0 s, both far short of the 8-minute threshold such a record would require where the record carries one, so the fare record supports no no-show fee.

The driver's post-hoc written claim that he waited at the pickup for over three minutes (F12) is contradicted by GPS and timeline records placing him 350 m away with 0 s inside the radius, so under the record-over-statement rule it cannot establish NS-1.

The chat is internally consistent with the rider's account rather than the driver's: the driver announced "Reached already" at 08:47 while 351 m away, the rider replied at 08:48 that she was at the pickup point with no car there, and the driver cancelled at 08:50 without ever having been in the 200 m radius.
There is no justification of the kind that would excuse the missed pickup: no traffic incidents near the route, no speed bands, and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain during the trip window.
Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail, the $6.61 charged on the fare record must be refunded in full to the rider rather than retained.

The driver is a long-tenured, clean record holder (1,346 days, 4.85 rating, 992 trips, 0 disputes upheld in 90 d), which is the only permissible use of profile facts here; a lenient outcome preserving his record and completion history is warranted.

weaknesses: The driver did press the "I'm Here" button (F5) and did wait 4 minutes stationary (F2), which looks like a genuine attempt to serve the trip; the counter-argument is simply that the button was pressed 351 m from the point (F5), so the formal NS-1 (ii) radius test is still failed.

The driver's own written statement (F12) says he waited at the pickup for over three minutes, and the other side will lean on the driver's 1,346-day, 4.85-rated clean profile (F17) to argue honest mistake rather than fee abuse; the answer is that F1/F2/F5 are system records and outrank the statement.

The rider's profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F16), which the other side may use to suggest she is claim-prone, but it is a profile fact and cannot decide the case; and no party claims any safety or threat issue, so no SAFE escalation is available to either side.

The 7-minute gap between acceptance (08:44) and cancellation (08:51) is short of the 8-minute sample threshold where a record carries one, so the driver cannot even argue he met a longer no-show clock (F3); the only route to keep the fee would be a GPS break, and F1-F5 show continuous coverage, so there is no G12 gap to exploit.

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while GPS placed him 351 m from the pickup point, so the arrival-confirmation requirement was not met.
The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point at any time — his closest approach was 319 m at 08:46:50 — and the platform recorded no arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null).
After tapping "I'm Here" the driver spent 0 seconds inside 200 m: he stood stationary from 08:47:00 to 08:51:00, about 350 m away, so the required continuous wait at the pickup point never occurred.
Because NS-1 (i)–(iii) all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not payable and must be refunded in full; the fee of $6.61 is the recorded charge (no surge applied).

The driver's "Reached already" message at 08:47 and his post-trip statement that he waited at the pickup are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (351 m from pickup at the tap, never inside 200 m), so on the system-record-priority rule they cannot establish a no-show.
The rider was at the pickup point and asked where the car was (chat #2, 08:48), and the driver cancelled at 08:51 anyway two minutes after that message — the rider did nothing that forfeits the fee.
Pressing "I'm Here" 351 m from the pickup to trigger a cancellation fee is an abuse of the cancellation/waiting button, so the account should additionally be sent for Ryde review.
Nothing in the record suggests a safety incident or a justified reason for the cancellation: no traffic incidents or congestion bands were recorded on the route and the weather was fair.

weaknesses: The rider filed one dispute in the last 90 days that was not upheld (F16), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of fee complaints, though it does not bear on this timeline.

The 'within 200 m' radius is a data-layer parameter (G2), not a published Ryde figure, so the driver could contest the exact metre threshold — but even a generous reading fails here since the closest approach was 319 m (F1).

claims.assertion: The $6.61 arose as a driver-cancelled no-show, so it can only stand if NS-1 (i)-(iii) are all satisfied; NS-0/NS-2 govern this branch.

NS-1 (ii) fails on the system records: the closest the driver ever came to the pickup point was 319 m at 08:46:50 and he was never within 200 m (F1), and the timeline never records driver_arrived_at the pickup (F4).

NS-1 (iii) also fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while 351 m from the pickup and then spent 0 s within 200 m, and his 4-minute stationary period (08:47:00-08:51:00) was at a point 350 m from the pickup, not at the pickup point.

The free-waiting period cannot rescue the fee either: the driver's patience ran only 7 minutes from acceptance (08:44:00) to cancellation (08:51:00) and the stationary wait was 4 min 0 s, both far short of the 8-minute threshold such a record would require where the record carries one, so the fare record supports no no-show fee.

The driver's post-hoc written claim that he waited at the pickup for over three minutes (F12) is contradicted by GPS and timeline records placing him 350 m away with 0 s inside the radius, so under the record-over-statement rule it cannot establish NS-1.

The chat is internally consistent with the rider's account rather than the driver's: the driver announced "Reached already" at 08:47 while 351 m away, the rider replied at 08:48 that she was at the pickup point with no car there, and the driver cancelled at 08:50 without ever having been in the 200 m radius.
There is no justification of the kind that would excuse the missed pickup: no traffic incidents near the route, no speed bands, and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain during the trip window.
Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail, the $6.61 charged on the fare record must be refunded in full to the rider rather than retained.

The driver is a long-tenured, clean record holder (1,346 days, 4.85 rating, 992 trips, 0 disputes upheld in 90 d), which is the only permissible use of profile facts here; a lenient outcome preserving his record and completion history is warranted.

weaknesses: The driver did press the "I'm Here" button (F5) and did wait 4 minutes stationary (F2), which looks like a genuine attempt to serve the trip; the counter-argument is simply that the button was pressed 351 m from the point (F5), so the formal NS-1 (ii) radius test is still failed.

The driver's own written statement (F12) says he waited at the pickup for over three minutes, and the other side will lean on the driver's 1,346-day, 4.85-rated clean profile (F17) to argue honest mistake rather than fee abuse; the answer is that F1/F2/F5 are system records and outrank the statement.

The rider's profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F16), which the other side may use to suggest she is claim-prone, but it is a profile fact and cannot decide the case; and no party claims any safety or threat issue, so no SAFE escalation is available to either side.

The 7-minute gap between acceptance (08:44) and cancellation (08:51) is short of the 8-minute sample threshold where a record carries one, so the driver cannot even argue he met a longer no-show clock (F3); the only route to keep the fee would be a GPS break, and F1-F5 show continuous coverage, so there is no G12 gap to exploit.
